text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone seeing it for the first time. One key idea is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so others can guess what they do. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When functions do too many things, the code becomes confusing and hard to fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because bugs are simpler to find and changes are safer to make. In short, writing clean code saves time for everyone on the team.
